summary.attribution: Written by a model from the explanatory memorandum; not the record
sentences: The bill would establish an independent Australian Federal Integrity Commission to prevent corruption and assess, investigate and report on serious or systemic corruption affecting Commonwealth administration.
Anyone could refer a corruption issue, while public hearings would require a public interest assessment considering seriousness, confidentiality, reputational harm and other relevant factors.
Historical conduct could be investigated subject to additional prevention-related requirements, with the laws and standards applicable when the conduct occurred governing its assessment.
changes: A Whistleblower Protection Commissioner would provide advice, practical support and assistance with proceedings concerning protected disclosures.
Commonwealth agencies would prepare integrity plans every two years covering at least the following four years.
A parliamentary committee and Parliamentary Inspector would oversee the commission.
People exonerated of a critical view tested at a public hearing would be entitled to a standalone report recording that finding.
summary.affected: Commonwealth agencies and public officials, whistleblowers, witnesses, people investigated and parliamentary oversight bodies would be affected.
